ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: the figure is a triangle ABC, B is above, A is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and AC is the base; point D is on side AB, and point E is on side BC; segment AE and CD intersect at F. The vertex angle ∠ABC is marked as 40°, and ∠EAB at A and ∠DCA at C are marked with the same arc, indicating that they are equal; what is required is ∠CFE at F formed by FC and FE. Reasoning: triangle ABC is an isosceles triangle, and the equal sides in the figure are AB and BC, so the base angles ∠BAC=∠BCA=(180°-40°)/2=70°. Let the equal marked angles ∠EAB=∠DCA=x. Because F is on AE, ∠FAC=∠BAC-∠EAB=70°-x; because F is on CD, ∠ACF=∠DCA=x. In triangle AFC, ∠AFC=180°-[(70°-x)+x]=110°. Also because A, F, E are collinear, ∠CFE and ∠AFC are supplementary angles, so ∠CFE=180°-110°=70°.

raw_record.question_text: The shown triangle $ABC$ is isosceles with $\measuredangle ABC=40^{\circ}$. The two indicated angles $\measuredangle EAB$ and $\measuredangle DCA$ are equal. How big is the angle $\measuredangle CFE$?

method.method_draft: Angle chase using the small triangle AFC. First read from the image that ABC has apex B at the top, base AC, points D on AB and E on BC, and cevians CD and AE intersect at F; the marked equal angles are at A between AE and AB and at C between DC and CA. From the text, ABC is isosceles and angle ABC is 40°, so with the image showing AB = BC as the equal sides, the base angles are angle BAC = angle BCA = 70°. Let the common marked angle be x: angle EAB = angle DCA = x. Then angle FAC = angle BAC - angle EAB = 70° - x, while angle ACF = angle DCA = x because F lies on CD. In triangle AFC, angle AFC = 180° - [(70° - x) + x] = 110°. Since A, F, E are collinear, angle CFE is supplementary to angle AFC, so angle CFE = 180° - 110° = 70°.
